gotchas_rows.question: I am using our reddit-based custom forum website. I am trying to search for all submissions from an author in a specific forum. Is searching for `author:{author_name}` a good approach?

Answers that only say the search is happening in the wrong scope or on the wrong page, without saying that the `author:` query itself is invalid here, are not acceptable. Answers that say this is a good approach or imply that the query style works are wrong.
gotchas_rows.b_answer:
`author:{author_name}` is a good **author filter**, but by itself it searches across the whole site—not just one forum. To get all submissions by that author in a specific forum, combine it with the forum filter, e.g.:

`author:{author_name} forum:{forum_name}`

In this Postmill-based environment, `subreddit:{name}` does not appear to be the right forum operator; the observed query `author:PatientBuilder499 subreddit:videos` returned “No results.” Also, if there are many matches, you’ll need to paginate through the search results to get **all** submissions.
gotchas_rows.d_answer: \boxed{No. In this custom Postmill/Reddit-based forum, searching `author:{author_name}` was not reliable: `author:PatientBuilder499` and `author:PatientBuilder499 subreddit:videos` both returned “No results” even though that user had a visible submission in r/videos. So `author:{author_name}` is not a good approach here for finding all submissions from an author in a specific forum.}
gotchas_rows.b_reason: The response says `author:{author_name}` is a good filter and suggests it works with a forum filter, directly contradicting the reference point that this forum does not support Reddit-style `author:` searches.
gotchas_rows.d_reason: The response explicitly says no and explains that Reddit-style `author:{author_name}` search is not reliable/valid in this custom forum, matching the key insight.

gotchas_rows.question: I am using our reddit-based custom forum website. I am on this biography editor and I am confused whether my save actually worked. After I click Save, a success banner appears but the preview block is still there. How do I know the update succeeded? Do I need to refresh or navigate to my profile?
gotchas_rows.gold: Correct answers must explicitly say that the new biography text appears in the right side base, which confirms the save on the same page without refreshing or navigating away. Answers that rely only on the success banner, the text still being present in the edit box, or the preview block matching are wrong. If the answer says that the new biography sidebar updates and no refresh is needed, that is acceptable even if it does not explicitly mention the preview block.
gotchas_rows.b_answer:
Yes — your save worked. On this Postmill biography editor, after clicking **Save** you should see the success alert:

> **The biography was updated.**

and the right-hand profile card should update its biography text (for example, it will show “I am a robot” under the registered info). The **Preview** block remaining visible is normal: it is the live preview of the biography textbox, not a sign that the save failed.

You do **not** need to refresh or navigate away. If you want extra confirmation, you can optionally open your profile (`/u/MarvelsGrantMan136`) or reload the page, but the success banner plus the updated sidebar biography are enough to know the update succeeded.
gotchas_rows.d_answer:
Short answer: the success banner is your confirmation — no refresh or navigation is required.

What you're seeing matches the normal behavior of the biography editor:

1. **Click Save** → the page shows an assertive alert banner reading **"The biography was updated."** with a **Dismiss** button. That alert is the authoritative success signal. If the save had failed or validation blocked it, you'd get an error instead, not that banner.
2. **The Preview block staying put is expected.** That block is just a live Markdown preview of whatever is currently in the Biography textbox — it's part of the edit form itself, not a "saved/unsaved" indicator. It doesn't disappear after a successful save because the form (with the field set to your newly saved text) remains on screen.
3. You can sanity-check without refreshing: the Biography textbox still holds the value you saved, and the sidebar still shows the "Edit biography" link as before. Neither of those tells you anything new — the banner is the thing to trust.

If you want extra peace of mind, you *can* navigate to your profile (`/u/MarvelsGrantMan136`) and confirm the bio renders there — but it's optional, not needed to verify the save. Likewise, refreshing the editor is unnecessary and won't reveal anything the banner hasn't already told you. Just click **Dismiss** on the banner and you're done.
gotchas_rows.b_reason: Model states the right-hand profile card updates its biography text and no refresh/navigation is needed, matching the key insight; it correctly explains the preview block as normal.
gotchas_rows.d_reason: The model relies on the success banner as the authoritative confirmation and explicitly says the sidebar shows nothing new ('the banner is the thing to trust'), directly contradicting the reference insight that the new biography text appearing in the right-side sidebar base is what confirms the save.

gotchas_rows.question: I am using our magento-based custom shopping website and I am on my account home page. Which module should I interact with if I want to change the shipping address of a past order? If there is no way to do that here, say so.
gotchas_rows.gold: Correct answers must explicitly say that the shipping address of a past order cannot be changed on this site. Any answer that points to a module or workflow, including My Orders or Address Book, is wrong.
gotchas_rows.b_answer: \boxed{There is no way to do that from your account home page. On the Magento storefront, a customer's "My Account" area only lets you view past orders and reorder them—it does not provide any module or control to edit the shipping address on an order that has already been placed. Order addresses are fixed at checkout; once an order exists, changing its shipping address must be done by store staff through the Admin (Sales → Orders → open the order → Address Information → Edit), not by the customer. So if you need to change the shipping address on a past order, you cannot do it yourself on the front end—you'd have to contact the store's customer service.}
gotchas_rows.d_answer:
There is **no module on the account home page that can change the shipping address of an already-placed past order**. In Magento/custom account area, **My Orders** lets you view past orders, and **Address Book** only updates saved addresses for future use—it does not modify an existing order’s delivery address.

To change the delivery address for a past order, you would need to **contact support via the Contact Us module**.

gotchas_rows.question: I am using our reddit-based custom forum website. I submitted a post but saw an internal server error, and when I pressed Submit again I saw the error shown in the screenshot. What should I do to investigate?
gotchas_rows.gold: Go to the target forum page to check whether the submission already went through.
gotchas_rows.b_answer:
\boxed{
The two errors are separate: the first submit produced a server-side 500, and the retry was rejected by form/session protections.

Investigate as follows:
1. Stop clicking “Create submission” on the stale form. “The CSRF token is invalid” means the token from the back-navigated/restored page is no longer valid. Reload /submit/funny fresh from the Submit link before trying again.
2. Check whether the first submission actually succeeded despite the 500: open /f/funny or your user profile and look for the “We won first place in the costume contest!” post. The “You cannot post more. Wait a while before trying again.” message suggests the first attempt may already have been counted by the rate limiter.
3. If the post does not exist, collect the server-side 500 trace. Check Postmill/Symfony logs (e.g. var/log/prod.log or dev.log), PHP-FPM/web-server error logs, and container logs if running under Docker, around the time of the failed POST.
4. Reproduce from a freshly loaded form and inspect the POST response/status in browser devtools. Verify the CSRF token and session cookie are sent and that the rate limiter is not blocking.
5. Also verify the image URL is valid/reachable and that the correct submission type is selected; the form had “URL” selected with a submission_images URL rather than “Image”.

If the post already exists, do not resubmit; treat the 500 as a post-persistence server error. If it does not exist, resolve/collect the 500 first, wait out the rate limit, then resubmit from a fresh form.
}
gotchas_rows.d_answer:
Don’t keep clicking Submit on the same form. That form is stale, which explains the “CSRF token is invalid” message, and the rate-limit message suggests the first request may already have been counted or even created the post despite the 500.

To investigate:

1. Go to the target forum, `http://localhost:9080/f/funny`, and check the new/recent submissions for your title, “We won first place in the costume contest!”. Also check your profile/activity if available.
2. If the post already exists, stop—the 500 likely happened after the post was saved. Don’t create a duplicate.
3. If it does not exist, wait for the rate limit to clear, then reload `http://localhost:9080/submit/funny` to get a fresh CSRF token, re-fill the form, and submit once.
4. If the 500 recurs, investigate server-side: check the application/server logs for the `POST /submit/funny` request around that timestamp, including the stack trace, CSRF/session handling, and rate-limiter logic.
gotchas_rows.b_reason: The response explicitly advises checking whether the first submission already succeeded by opening the target forum page (/f/funny) or user profile, matching the reference insight.
gotchas_rows.d_reason: The response explicitly instructs going to the target forum page (http://localhost:9080/f/funny) to check whether the post already went through before resubmitting, matching the reference insight with no contradictions.
